criteria.name: Q1 Quality attributes
criteria.reasoning: Two relevant attributes justified from lunch-peak scenario. Performance scenario is six-part and measurable. Availability scenario has six parts but response measure is not measurable.

evidence.quote: the system should stay up most of the time.

criteria.name: Q2 Architectural style
criteria.reasoning: Clear modular-monolith recommendation. Two scenario-specific trade-offs: 5-person team vs overhead, single VM and deployment downtime fixes. Downside explicitly acknowledged.

evidence.quote: a bug in one module can still crash the whole process.

criteria.name: Q3 Availability calculation
criteria.reasoning: Part (a) correct. Part (b) arithmetic wrong: 0.00699x720 is ~5.0h not 3.5h. Part (c) wrong: uses payment-only 99.9975% not series ~99.80% and downtime ~1.5h.

criteria.name: Q4 Resilience pattern
criteria.reasoning: Appropriate pattern chosen and applied, but open/closed states inverted, so mechanism explained incorrectly. No clear drawback or tuning trade-off stated.

evidence.quote: In the Open state calls pass through normally.

criteria.name: Q5 Consistency and availability
criteria.reasoning: Both availability vs consistency choices reasonable. Menu technique named (Redis TTL). Payment technique missing and CAP misused; partition tolerance cannot be given up.

evidence.quote: for payments we choose consistency and availability and give up partition tolerance.

criteria.name: Q6 Architecture decision record
criteria.reasoning: Context, Decision, Consequences present and specific to outlet notification. Multiple positives given but no negative consequence, cost or complexity.

evidence.quote: The queue also smooths the lunch peak because the workers process orders

criteria.name: Communication and format
criteria.reasoning: Clear writing with required headings, but [2] cited in Q4 missing from list, no assumptions stated, and Q2 likely exceeds 150-word limit.

evidence.quote: [1] L. Bass, P. Clements, and R. Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice,

technical_issues.issue: Circuit breaker states reversed: Closed is normal operation, Open fails fast, Half-Open trials
CAP: partition tolerance is mandatory during partition; choice is between C and A, cannot sacrifice P

overall: Good architectural judgment for style and ADR, but undermined by availability calculation errors, inverted breaker states, and CAP error.

feedback.summary: You showed good judgment on style and trade-offs, with clear scenarios for performance and a solid ADR. To improve, you need measurable response measures, correct availability maths, accurate pattern and CAP explanations, and balanced consequences with precise formatting.
next_steps: Rewrite vague measures and add missing negative consequence, payment technique, and breaker tuning.
Recalculate Q3(b)-(c) as full series with working and fix inverted Open/Closed breaker states and CAP claim.
Keep all answers under 150 words and complete your IEEE list, including [2] from Q4.

criteria.C1: You did well in Question 1 choosing two relevant attributes with lunch-peak justification and a measurable performance scenario. To reach Excellent, rewrite your availability measure — 'stay up most of the time' is not measurable — as a quantified target.
criteria.C2: You excelled in Question 2 with a clear modular-monolith recommendation, two scenario-specific trade-offs on 5-person team and single VM downtime, and acknowledged that 'a bug in one module can still crash the whole process.'
criteria.C3: You showed correct method in Question 3(a). To move up, fix Question 3(b) to ~5.0h and Question 3(c) to end-to-end series ~99.80% with ~1.5h downtime, showing working to requested precision.
criteria.C4: You picked an appropriate pattern for the Question 4 outage. To progress, correct your states — you wrote 'In the Open state calls pass through normally' — to Closed normal, Open fail-fast, Half-Open trials, plus a drawback.
criteria.C5: You made reasonable choices in Question 5 and named Redis TTL for menus. For Excellent, correct CAP — you cannot give up partition tolerance — and name a concrete payment technique.
criteria.C6: You wrote specific Context, Decision and Consequences for outlet notification with good positives on lunch-peak smoothing. To reach Excellent, add at least one negative consequence like cost or complexity.
criteria.C7: Your writing is clear with required headings. For Excellent, keep every answer within 150 words (check Q2), add missing reference [2] cited in Q4 to your list, and state assumptions.
